Red: M(21,21)=R1, Y(21,27)=R2, N(21,39)=R4, R3 is empty.

So the last swap (G4↔R3) didn't happen! The batch executed 5 actions: 4 clicks + SPACE. But wait — the swap (G3,R4) did happen: G3=N↔R4=R → G3=R, R4=N ✓. Then the click (36,39) G4=b, (22,34) R3=empty… and SPACE. Hmm, but R3 is still empty and G4 is still b. So the swap of G4 with the empty R3… when you click an empty slot, maybe nothing gets selected (you can't select an empty slot), so the second click (22,34) did nothing, and then SPACE was pressed.
So the current state differs from P1's target: b is at G4 instead of R3. P1 requires R3=b, G4=empty.
Wait, but hold on — did SPACE even evaluate in the first place? The board changed (board_changed True) — but that's because of the swap. The level didn't complete. But wait, was SPACE evaluated with G4=b, R3=empty? If P1 is the correct answer, then with b at G4 (wrong slot) it should fail.
Hmm, but actually — maybe the game doesn't allow clicking on empty slots. So to move b from G4 to R3, I need to swap G4 with a slot that has a piece… but R3 is empty. How do I move a piece into an empty slot? In level 1, were there empty slots? No, level 1 was 4 pieces in 4 slots. Hmm, in level 2 the initial state was: 7 pieces in 8 slots, with R3 empty from the start. And in previous turns I moved pieces around… did I ever move a piece into R3? Let me check the history. In the first attempt (green first), the state was red: N(22), Y(28), M(40) — R3 was empty. In the current attempt R3 is still empty. So R3 has been empty the whole time, and I've never moved a piece into R3!
Wait, that's a problem: if R3 is a sequence slot that needs to be filled (as in P1), then I need to move a piece into R3. Can I? Clicking an empty slot might not work. Or maybe clicking an empty slot works and swaps (moves) the piece there.
Let me test: click G4 (b at 36,39), then click R3 (22,34). If b moves to R3, then empty slots are selectable. Let me try that and observe.
Actually wait — in the last batch, the clicks (36,39) and (22,34) were executed, and then SPACE. The result: G4 is still b, R3 is still empty. So either:
(a) Clicking an empty slot does nothing (the swap wasn't registered), or
(b) The swap happened and then… no, b is still at G4.
So (a): empty slots can't be selected. Hmm. Then how do I put a piece into R3?
Maybe… R3 isn't a slot at all! Maybe the green square is just a pipe mouth (decoration), not a slot. Then the sequence is 7 slots: G1–G4, R1, R2, R4. And the reading order is… my first attempt (G=O,p,R,b; R1=N,R2=Y,R4=M) failed. The second (R1=O,R2=p,R4=R; G=b,N,Y,M) also failed.
Hmm, so if R3 isn't a slot, the order must be something else: for example G1,G2,G3,G4,R4,R2,R1 or R4,R3… no, that's wrong.
Wait, wait. Let me re-verify: was the first attempt really correct? Let me re-verify from the history what state was in place when I pressed SPACE the first time in level 2. Let me examine the history transitions around the level 2 SPACE actions.
